message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
The two lineages diverged very early in mammalian evolution, so their most recent common ancestor is not a modern animal but a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene.  

That ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. In other words, the lion and zebra share a common ancestor that was a primitive Laurasiatherian mammal, not a specific modern species.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla. Actually, lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla. So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps a placental mammal ancestor. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the eutherian ancestor. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both orders, which is the clade of Laurasiatheria? Actually, Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of the clade Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would be a small mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene, the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. Alternatively, the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But the question likely expects "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which is a small mammal that lived about 70-80 million years ago." So answer accordingly. No tool needed.
